transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recorded via Fireflies

Attendees:
- Sophie Clarke (Redwood, AE)
- Miguel Alvarez (Redwood, SE)
- Diane Park (Beacon, Head of Procurement)
- Arjun Patel (Beacon, Engineering Manager)
- Lisa Nguyen (Beacon, Counsel)
- Trevor Mills (Beacon, FinOps)
- Maya Chen (Beacon, Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Kickoff to align legal and commercial path for onboarding Redwood for inference services. Main asks: MSA redlines, DPA scoping, SLA commitments for 99th/95th p99 latency targets, pricing tiers and egress/egress-fees clarity.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick run through the contract and pricing posture and then miguel will jump into the technical bits, sound good?
[00:08] Diane: yes that works, thanks Sophie. we've got counsel on the call because of some DPA questions and then trevor is here for the pricing side.
[00:15] Arjun: hi everyone sorry slightly delayed, i'm here.
[00:18] Miguel: no worries. quick note, timestamps in the notes might drift a bit my mic is picking up a lot.
[00:26] Sophie: ok cool. high level agenda: 1) commercial ask and procurement path; 2) MSA redline overview; 3) DPA / data residency; 4) SLA and pricing variance discussion; 5) next steps.

[05:10] Sophie: on the MSA, beacon asked for a few clarifications in section 6 and 9 around indemnity and liability cap - standard request - we propose a $X million cap tied to monthly committed spend, but open to equivalence based on committed capacity. open question is whether you want a per-incident cap or aggregate cap.
[05:38] Lisa: right, most legal teams prefer an aggregate, but we have to check with our insurance. also want stronger audit log language, and retention windows spelled out in the DPA.
[05:48] Sophie: yeah we can give a clarified audit logging clause. our platform does token-level logging but you can opt out and use private deployment, that removes logs from our control, right miguel?
[05:59] Miguel: yes if you run Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS and no central logging, you control retention. there is a small ops footprint if you want hosted console for observability we can mask or filter tokens, but egress is constrained.
[06:25] Maya: on security side, can you confirm KMS integrations: do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM? and is there a bring-your-own-key option for hosted?
[06:36] Miguel: we support AWS and GCP KMS natively; BYOK for hosted is available under enterprise tier with double-wrap and HSM integration via our private connectors. caveat: full BYOK for hosted requires a dedicated private deployment in the VPC option.

[10:02] Trevor: pricing, we are looking at committed capacity vs burst. our finance team wants to understand the delta for egress fees and token accounting for embeddings vs generation. in our model embeddings volume is huge so we need a different rate.
[10:24] Sophie: right, embeddings are priced differently; we'll send the detailed workbook. quick note: we have three pricing levers - committed reserved capacity (monthly commit), on-demand bursts, and per-token API for hosted. embedding units use a per-embedding unit metric and we have bulk discounts.
[10:45] Trevor: ok can you itemize egress? we sometimes get surprised by cross-region egress in other vendors.
[10:53] Miguel: we have a clear egress table - cross-region data transfer for private deployments is customer network cost; for hosted, we apply a small egress fee for large volume exports, but usually it's small relative to compute. i'll add the exact line items in the workbook.

[15:30] Diane: procurement process question: what's the typical procurement committee review time once we provide the annotated MSA? we have a 2-week window to close with stakeholders.
[15:39] Sophie: in our experience procurement+legal typically take 7-14 business days assuming no major redlines; if there are SOC2/DPA exceptions that can extend. we try to be responsive and have an AE+SE triage to speed it up.
[15:50] Lisa: our main DPA ask is residency — eu only for a subset of data and a list of restricted countries. also need to see flow diagrams of telemetry and logs.
[16:02] Miguel: we can provide architecture diagrams showing where KV cache lives, what gets logged, and the routing policies for smart routing. (note: in the transcript KV cache sometimes auto-transcribed as K V cash).

[20:11] Sophie: on SLA, we offer tiered SLAs by product path: hosted standard (99.5% uptime), dedicated with reserved capacity (SLA bumped with latency targets for p95/p99) and private full enterprise SLA. The key piece Beacon asked about is latency SLO for inference - what p95/p99 do you need?
[20:30] Arjun: for user-facing features we'd like p95 < 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) and p99 < 600ms ideally, is that achievable?
[20:41] Miguel: depends on model and quantization, but with Dedicated and model quantization profiles we can typically hit p95 ~150-250ms on Llama-like small-medium models; p99 can spike with cache misses but we have prefix caching and KV cache reuse strategies to reduce that. i'll prepare a short benchmark note with numbers observed in similar workloads.

[25:05] Arjun: what's the fallback plan if dedicated capacity nodes are saturated during business hours? we can't have production falling back to much higher latency.
[25:17] Miguel: we have smart routing and automatic fallback tiers: primary dedicated pool, then burst capacity within same region, then hosted-compatible variant that is cheaper but slightly higher latency. we can set canary policies to failover gracefully. you can also pin model variants to keep latency predictable.

[30:00] Trevor: price shock scenario — if we exceed committed tokens due to a marketing burst, what's the surcharge?
[30:12] Sophie: surcharge rates are spelled in the workbook; typical approach is an overage rate per token or per-embedding unit, or we can negotiate a temporary burst cap with a blended rate. we can also do auto-notify when usage hits 80/90% of commit to avoid surprises.
[30:35] Diane: would the auto-notify go to our FinOps and Procurement emails? we'd want a two-person ack before surcharging.
[30:43] Sophie: yes we can configure alerting to multiple recipients and require an acknowledgement before billing a burst above X%.

[35:40] Lisa: a couple of legal nuances — can you confirm incident disclosure timelines and whether you will provide a SOC 2 attestation prior to contract?
[35:52] Sophie: we provide SOC 2 Type II attestation as part of the security pack. incident notification windows are 24 hours for critical incidents; data breaches that materially affect customer data have contractual notification timelines in the DPA.
[36:10] Maya: for technical preflight, we'll need the endpoint IP ranges for allow-listing and a runbook for key rotation.
[36:20] Miguel: we'll send the IP CIDR ranges and a key rotation doc; for hosted BYOK we require a private connector and we'll coordinate with your infra team.

[40:00] Diane: procurement wants to understand acceptance criteria for go-live. we prefer a production acceptance test with a run-for-7-days and a performance acceptance matrix.
[40:15] Miguel: we can do a pilot: 2-week pilot with a small dedicated pool, us supporting a weekly check-in, and defined SLO measurements. if performance is within agreed thresholds we move to prod and scale commit.
[40:30] Trevor: ok what about data retention for logs and traces? we need 90 days for audit but redaction for PII.
[40:40] Sophie: default audit logs are 90 days, we can extend retention for enterprise packs. we also support token-level redaction and can provide a scrubbed logging mode.

[45:55] Arjun: integration question: is the SDK going to require our engineers to rewrite CLI? we are using k8s and have a service mesh; how invasive is the integration?
[46:08] Miguel: SDKs are lightweight. for Dedicated we provide a helm chart and a sidecar example; for private deployments it's largely self-managed and integrates with your k8s. most teams take 2-3 sprints to integrate depending on complexity.

[50:10] Sophie: circling back to commercial path, we'll attach an annotated MSA with our suggested compromise language on liability, plus a DPA draft with residency options and an appendix listing SLA tiers. we'll also attach a workbook that breaks pricing into committed vs burst vs embedding rates.
[50:26] Diane: excellent. can you also include a short memo about alternative model variants and quantization tradeoffs so our ML team can review cost/quality?
[50:35] Miguel: yes i'll include that — short bullet summary and observed token costs for common configs.

[55:00] Lisa: small ask — can you confirm whether Redwood will accept DPAs with a limited subprocessor list and if they allow subprocessors to be named in an appendix rather than in the body?
[55:12] Sophie: yes we typically put subprocessors in an appendix and allow customers to review them; for private deployment you can avoid subprocessors entirely since you manage infra, for hosted we keep a standard list and can include a notification process for additions.

[58:30] Sophie: ok to recap: Sophie will send annotated MSA + pricing workbook + security pack by Friday 2026-03-06; Miguel will send latency benchmarks and canary rollout notes by Monday 2026-03-09; Beacon will confirm procurement committee slot for 2026-03-11 and Lisa will send DPA exceptions and residency list by 2026-03-07.
[58:55] Diane: that sounds right. thanks all.
[59:03] Trevor: quick finance note, please flag any minimums or early termination fees in the pricing spreadsheet.
[59:12] Sophie: will do, i'll bold those lines.
[59:20] Arjun: thanks everyone, looking forward to the pilot.
[59:25] Miguel: thanks, i'll follow up with the technical docs.
[59:30] Sophie: great, we'll adjourn. thanks for your time.
